Its H3x exhibit then showed the one thing that history cannot see about itself. Replace the whole history file with an older, internally consistent copy and everything the store checks passes — the chain re-hashes, the head matches its newest row, the bound writer agrees with the old file — and recovery installs a stale state. GPT's ruling on R6.3 makes that the round:
A self-consistent Locus history is not sufficient evidence that it is the current Locus history.
Recovery may use a history head only when a deployment-controlled anchor establishes that exact head and writer binding as current.
